topics.sampleQuestion: Which marketing channel should my SaaS start with?

principles.text: Fix market, product, business model and messaging first; channels come last, or none of them will work.
Use payback period, not LTV:CAC, to set acquisition spend; aim for 3 to 6 months, ideally under a year.
Point rented and borrowed channels back to owned ones: newsletter, RSS feed, personal site, community or text list.
Turn repeated SOPs into skills, with one product-marketing context file that every other skill reads first.
Pick one simple starting price, avoid ultra-low $9/mo pricing, and test new pricing on new customers first.

sampleQA.question: How should I price my early-stage SaaS?

answer.text: Don't over-engineer it. Pick one monthly or annual price low enough that about 75% of users wouldn't balk, but high enough that they have to think about it.
Make it competitive with alternatives rather than cost-plus, and anchor it to the value metric that tracks how customers get value.
Resist ultra-low pricing like $9/mo. It creates false traction and is hard to raise 5-10x later.
Test new pricing on new customers only, for roughly 3 to 6 months, since existing customers are anchored to their old price.

sampleQA.question: Which marketing channel should I start with?

answer.text: He starts with SEO, which now includes AEO, then moves to Google Ads, then Meta, and stops when he hits resistance.
Direct sales outreach, SEO, ads and partnerships are the best first channels. SEO stands out because it is predictable, free and compounds.
Before any channel, get market, product, business model and messaging working, or no channel will work.
Run only one to three growth experiments at a time so you can isolate and trust the results.

sampleQA.question: How do I get my product recommended by ChatGPT and other AI assistants?

answer.text: Good AEO is good SEO first, plus good product marketing and a broad footprint of mentions across the web.
Write extractable content where each key claim stands alone, and add sourced stats. Keyword stuffing lowers AI visibility.
Being cited is not being recommended: shortlists lean on reviews, forums and press. Put pricing in readable text so agents don't skip you.
Measure with repeated runs and mention rates. One run is an anecdote, not a measurement.
